pins.name: D8
pins.label: D8 (GPIO8)
pins.notes: PIN_SERIAL2_TX (D8) — feeds the DI (driver input) pin of the onboard MAX33072E RS-485 transceiver (U14), which drives CN17's RJ45 connector for BRT LDSBus/DMX512 control. Confirmed via IDM2040-7A datasheet Figure 15 'RS-485 Transceiver with Polarity Control'. Unlike the sibling bridgetek_idm2040_43a (which has no RS-485 hardware and leaves this GPIO general-purpose), this GPIO is permanently committed on the 7A. Sketches still use it normally via Serial2 for the RS-485/LDSBus/DMX512 feature itself — this override only removes it from the Designer's generic digital/PWM pin-picker pool.

pins.name: D9
pins.label: D9 (GPIO9)
pins.notes: PIN_SERIAL2_RX (D9) — fed by the RO (receiver output) pin of the onboard MAX33072E RS-485 transceiver (U14). Same reasoning and datasheet source as GPIO8.

pins.name: D16
pins.label: D16 (GPIO16)
pins.notes: D16 — datasheet-confirmed UART1_POL: RS-485 A/B polarity-select output for the onboard MAX33072E transceiver, driven by RP2040 GP16 per CN17's own description ('the polarity of RS-485 A/B signal can be controlled by RP2040 GP16... Low for LDSBus... High for DMX512') and reiterated in section 7.2. Permanently wired to onboard hardware, not a general-purpose spare pin.

pins.name: GPIO25
pins.label: GPIO25 (Led active high)
pins.notes:
PIN_LED — onboard status LED. Standard unmodified Raspberry Pi Pico-form-factor LED circuit (470R resistor to a GREEN LED per the datasheet's own schematic), confirmed active-high per the rpipico/wiznet_5500_evb_pico/bridgetek_idm2040_43a precedent; also appears as a LED output in the datasheet's own MicroPython/CircuitPython blink example code (Pin(25,Pin.OUT) / board.GP25).
Check if available on board

pins.name: A1
pins.label: A1 (GPIO27)
pins.notes: A1 (D-alias not declared, but GPIO27 is the analog-capable 'A1' pin per this board's own pins_arduino.h; also the vendor's unused PIN_WIRE1_SCL #define) — datasheet schematic identifies this GPIO's net as UART1_DE: the driver-enable control line for the onboard MAX33072E RS-485 transceiver (Figure 15). Not exposed on CN5's external header (only GPIO26/A0 is), corroborating it is internally committed rather than general-purpose. Permanently wired to onboard hardware — override removes it from the Designer's analog/digital/PWM pin-picker pool.

pins.name: A2
pins.label: A2 (GPIO28)
pins.notes: A2 (D-alias not declared, but GPIO28 is the analog-capable 'A2' pin per this board's own pins_arduino.h) — datasheet schematic identifies this GPIO's net as CARD_DET#: the onboard microSD card socket (CN4)'s card-detect switch line ('CN4 is a Micro SD card socket... The physical interface supports the card detection'). Note this board's own `#define SDCARD_DETECT 33` in pins_arduino.h is an inert placeholder (GPIO33 is outside the RP2040's valid 0-29 GPIO range) — the real card-detect signal is this GPIO, not the value that macro names. Permanently wired to onboard hardware, not general-purpose.
